headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,060-4,088 AS NFP WEEK OPENS — US-Iran Floor + Central Bank Bid Keeps Bulls Alive; JOLTS, ADP, Friday Payrolls In View
snippet: Gold is holding firm at $4,060–$4,088/oz on Tuesday August 4 as the week's macro gauntlet begins — JOLTS job openings today, ADP private payrolls Wednesday, and the critical July nonfarm payrolls report on Friday — with US-Iran tensions (Washington paused but has not cancelled planned airstrikes) providing a geopolitical bid that has prevented a retest of the $4,022 intraday low. Silver rose 1.83% to $58.74/oz. Analysts note that gold's resilience above $4,060 into a data-heavy week, combined with last week's hawkish 9-3 Fed vote and a two-thirds probability of a September rate hike, reflects the structural demand floor from central bank accumulation that has absorbed every macro-driven selloff since Q1.

headline: WGC BOMBSHELL: CENTRAL BANKS BUY RECORD 289 TONNES IN Q2 — Poland 51t, China 33t; Buying INTO A 16% Price DROP; Strongest Q2 On Record
snippet: The World Gold Council's Q2 2026 Gold Demand Trends report, released July 30, confirmed that central banks purchased a record 289 tonnes in Q2 2026 — up 74% year-on-year and the strongest second-quarter official buying on record — with Poland leading at 51 tonnes (total reserves now 632 tonnes) and the People's Bank of China adding 33 tonnes, its largest quarterly purchase since Q4 2023. The critical detail: this record buying occurred into a quarter when gold prices fell approximately 16%, the worst quarterly performance since 2013 — meaning sovereign buyers are explicitly treating price weakness as a buying opportunity. Also notable: jewelry demand fell 17% at elevated prices, but coin/bar and ETF demand more than compensated, and investment demand is now structurally the dominant driver of marginal price discovery.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT DEEPENS — 46.3-Moz Gap In 2026 As Solar Makers CUT But Retail HOARDS; Coin/Bar Demand Up 18%
snippet: The silver market is tracking for its sixth consecutive structural supply deficit in 2026, with the Silver Institute projecting a 46.3-million-ounce shortfall — a 15% widening from 40.3 Moz in 2025 — as industrial users retreat and retail buyers accelerate in opposite directions. Industrial demand is down 3% to 639.6 Moz as solar panel and jewelry manufacturers cut silver use at sustained high prices, but retail coin and bar demand has surged 18% to its highest level since 2022, while ETF inflows add to investment-side pressure. Because most silver is mined as a gold, copper, and zinc byproduct rather than primary production, higher prices don't automatically produce more metal — leaving the market structurally dependent on continued drawdowns of above-ground inventory to bridge the supply-demand gap.

headline: GALLEON GOLD 19.45m AT 6.8 g/t Au NAILS ZONE 9 CORE — Includes 6.15m AT 16.84 g/t; 500m Down-Dip Continuity Confirmed At Timmins (TSX-V: GGO)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Galleon Gold Corp
snippet: Galleon Gold Corp (TSX-V: GGO) reported July 30, 2026 that hole WC-26-241 at its West Cache gold project in Timmins, Ontario returned 19.45 metres at 6.8 g/t Au — including 6.15 metres at 16.84 g/t Au — within a broader 29.05-metre interval averaging 4.72 g/t, confirming the high-grade structural core of Zone 9 and demonstrating down-dip continuity to approximately 500 metres depth. With 11,500 metres completed of its 18,000-metre 2026 drill campaign across the South Zone and Zone 9, Galleon has systematically de-risked the deposit geometry through 21 holes — the kind of methodical, grade-consistent intercept sequence that underpins a meaningful resource upgrade rather than an isolated headline result.

headline: ANGLO TECK ADVANCES TO CLOSE — Teck Launches Bond Consent Solicitation August 3; China/South Korea Now The Final Gate; Top-5 Copper Producer Forming (TSX: TECK)
snippet: Teck Resources (TSX/NYSE: TECK) commenced consent solicitation from its bond holders on August 3, 2026 — a key mechanical step toward closing its C$53 billion merger-of-equals with Anglo American to form Anglo Teck, a Canadian-headquartered global critical minerals champion with 70%+ copper exposure and top-5 global copper producer status. The Anglo Teck executive leadership team was announced July 30 alongside US$800 million in synergy targets; final regulatory approvals from China and South Korea are the remaining conditions, expected between September 2026 and March 2027. For copper junior investors, the pending creation of Anglo Teck — the largest copper-centric company in the Western world — is a structural event that compresses implied takeover premiums across the copper developer and mid-tier space as the new entity's M&A mandate comes into focus.

headline: HOT CHILI AT DIGGERS AUGUST 4 — La Verde 400m x 400m Near-Surface Copper-Gold Zone; CEO Easterday Presents As ASX Tightens Disclosure Scrutiny (ASX/TSX-V: HCH)
snippet: Hot Chili Limited (ASX/TSX-V: HCH) CEO Christian Easterday presented at Diggers & Dealers 2026 in Kalgoorlie at 11:20am on August 4 — the same week the company amended its July 2026 investor presentation after the ASX required removal of a slide showing in-situ resource valuations without adequate compliance framing. The amended presentation highlights the La Verde copper-gold discovery 35 km from the Costa Fuego hub, where 11 drillholes have defined a 400m x 400m high-grade near-surface starter pit zone with multiple intercepts above 0.6% CuEq within 200 metres of surface and near-road access. The ASX compliance action is a signal that regulators are tightening disclosure standards on junior mining resource communications — a backdrop relevant to any TSX-V investor evaluating in-situ value claims in project marketing materials.

headline: EVOLUTION MINING CEO AT DIGGERS: CONSENSUS LT GOLD NOW $3,650/oz — Up FROM $1,800 In 2024; The Re-Rating Math Has Changed For Every Junior (ASX: EVN)
snippet: Evolution Mining (ASX: EVN) CEO Lawrie Conway presented at Diggers & Dealers 2026 on August 3, citing consensus long-term gold price forecasts rising from USD $1,800/oz in 2024 to USD $3,650/oz (approximately AUD $5,224/oz) in 2026 — an observation that has direct implications for the entire junior mining sector. The consensus long-term price is the single most important input in project economic models: when consultants and institutional analysts raise their long-run gold assumption from $1,800 to $3,650, every NPV, IRR, and acquisition premium in the sector re-prices accordingly. For TSX-V junior investors, this means projects that were marginal or sub-economic at $2,000/oz gold now carry fundamentally different financial profiles — and that the re-rating window for well-defined gold development assets may be structurally earlier in the price cycle than historical precedent suggests.

headline: LYNAS TEXAS RARE EARTH PLANT 'MAY NOT PROCEED' — DoD Offtake Talks Stall; America First PIVOTS To MP Materials; Western Heavy REE Chain At Risk (ASX: LYC)
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) CEO Amanda Lacaze has warned the company's DoD-funded Seadrift, Texas heavy rare earth separation facility 'might not proceed' after negotiations with the US Department of Defense failed to reach a mutually acceptable offtake agreement on commercial terms — a significant setback for US efforts to build a domestic ex-China dysprosium and terbium supply chain. The failure reflects Washington's America First policy pivot that directed a multibillion-dollar DoD partnership and government equity stake to domestic rival MP Materials, effectively sidelining Lynas despite its Seadrift plant being physically under construction. The potential cancellation of the Seadrift facility increases Western exposure to Chinese-controlled heavy rare earth supply at a moment when China's REE export controls are actively disrupting global magnet supply chains for EV motors and defense systems.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $86.63/LB AS SPROTT TRUST ACCUMULATES 79M POUNDS — Spot Floor Established; Contracting Cycle Absorbing Kazakh Output Growth
snippet: Uranium spot held at US$86.63 per pound as of August 3, 2026 — comfortably above the $80 threshold multiple developers cite as their project economics baseline — with the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust now holding approximately 79 million pounds of U3O8 as institutional accumulation persists despite moderation from the early-year high above $100/lb. Kazatomprom's H1 2026 output growth of 9% year-on-year to 13,291 tonnes has not broken the $85-$90 spot floor because the utility re-contracting cycle is absorbing incremental Kazakh production into a term market that remains structurally undersupplied — a dynamic particularly relevant for Western uranium developers whose project economics require sustained $85+ spot to attract construction financing.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.47/LB AS JP MORGAN PROJECTS 330,000t DEFICIT — Ore Grades At 50-YEAR LOWS; AI Data Center Demand Alone 475,000t In 2026
snippet: Copper held at US$6.47 per pound on August 3-4, 2026 — up 45.8% year-over-year — as JP Morgan's 2026 projection of a 330,000-tonne refined deficit confronts a supply-side grade crisis where Chilean and Peruvian ore grades have fallen below 0.6%, half the level of 25 years ago, forcing miners to process exponentially more rock to extract the same copper. On the demand side, JP Morgan estimates AI data centers alone will require approximately 475,000 tonnes of copper in 2026 — a category that barely existed three years ago — compounding the structural demand growth from EVs and grid infrastructure. For TSX-V and ASX copper junior investors, the combination of a multi-decade grade decline and AI-driven demand step-change is the structural demand-supply dynamic that justifies premium valuations for high-grade new copper discoveries in low-risk jurisdictions.

headline: ALKANE RESOURCES AT DIGGERS: 160,000+ oz EQ/YR ON TRACK — COSTERFIELD ANTIMONY Adds Critical Mineral Angle Post-Mandalay Integration (ASX/TSX: ALK)
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX/TSX: ALK) presented at Diggers & Dealers 2026 on August 3, confirming its three-mine portfolio — Tomingley (NSW gold), Costerfield (Victoria gold-antimony), and Björkdal (Sweden gold) — is on track to deliver over 160,000 gold-equivalent ounces in FY2026, with a pathway to 180,000 oz the following year and a pro-forma cash balance of approximately A$218 million following the completed Mandalay Resources integration. The Costerfield mine's antimony co-product adds an under-appreciated critical mineral dimension: antimony has surged in value due to US and Chinese export control dynamics, and Costerfield is one of the few operating mines in the Western world producing antimony outside of Chinese jurisdiction — giving Alkane exposure to a US-designated strategic mineral within an existing cash-generating operation.
